pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING - FICTIONAL AND NON-FICTIONAL

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we relate events in a text with real life, people or places?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension
2. respond to texts correctly for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING - FICTIONAL AND NON-FICTIONAL
This lesson teaches Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional for Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. respond to texts correctly for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional above.
2. Explain Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we relate events in a text with real life, people or places?
2. How can we predict what will happen in a text or story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. create mental images from viewed, heard or read text for comprehension
2. respond to texts correctly for comprehension

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
